key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, moderate thermal gradients and stabilize axial forces in HDPE joining.
method: Model heat transfer, material flow and defect formation using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian simulation.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Use simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good agreement with CEL predictions; ANN temperature and force predictions achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy is demonstrated within the tested parameter space; transfer to other HDPE grades, tool geometries or welding conditions requires further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
